comprehensiveness.criterion: The report covers legal frameworks for ADAS liability in multiple jurisdictions.
The report discusses existing precedents, case law, and regulatory guidance.
The report addresses the human-machine control handoff problem and its legal implications.
The report covers policy debates, industry standards, and proposed reforms.

insight.criterion: The report evaluates strengths and limitations of different approaches rather than merely summarizing them.
The report identifies open questions, recent developments, or ongoing debates in the field.
The report draws connections between theoretical results and practical implications.
The report provides critical commentary on the assumptions underlying different models or claims.

instruction_following.criterion: The report directly answers the research question posed in the task instruction.
The report includes a Sources section listing references and consulted materials.
The report is substantive (at least 2000 words) demonstrating thorough research.
The report is written in well-structured markdown with clear sections and subsections.

readability.criterion: The report has a clear logical flow and coherent narrative from introduction to conclusion.
Technical terminology and notation are used correctly and explained where necessary.
Sections are well-organized with descriptive headers and appropriate use of formatting.
The writing is clear, concise, and accessible to an informed reader without unnecessary jargon.
